title: Air and Water Resistance
seo_title: Year 5 Science: Air and Water Resistance Worksheets (Parachutes and Streamlining)
standard_text: Identify the effects of air resistance, water resistance and friction, that act between moving surfaces.
meta_desc: Free Year 5 science worksheets on air and water resistance: parachute investigations, falling shapes in water, streamlined animals and vehicles, and forces on falling objects. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Big surfaces feel more resistance; streamlined shapes slip through.
body_html:
How to think about it

Air and water push against moving objects and slow them down.

  • Air resistance and water resistance act against the direction of movement.
  • A bigger area means more resistance: a bigger parachute falls more slowly.
  • Streamlined shapes (dolphins, racing cars, fish) reduce resistance so they move faster.
Example

A ball falls. Air resistance acts?

Against the movement

Answer: upwards

Example

10 cm or 40 cm parachute: slower?

More area, more air resistance

Answer: 40 cm

Common mistakes

  • Thinking resistance pushes in the direction of movement.
  • Thinking a bigger parachute falls faster.
  • Thinking streamlined means heavier.

faq.a: A force from the air that acts against objects moving through it. It slows falling objects and moving vehicles.

faq.q: Why does a bigger parachute fall more slowly?
faq.a: It has a bigger area, so more air pushes against it and there is more air resistance.
Having a smooth, pointed shape that lets air or water flow past easily, so there is less resistance.

items.q: What does streamlined mean?
c: shaped so that air or water flows past easily

items.q: What is water resistance?
c: a force that makes things float
a force from water that pushes against objects moving through it

items.q: Why does this happen: a skydiver opening a parachute?
c: to reduce air resistance and go faster
to reduce friction with the ground
to increase air resistance and slow down

items.q: When a parachute falls at a steady speed, what is true about the forces?
c: Air resistance balances the pull of gravity.

items.q: How is a penguin swimming designed or adapted to go fast?
c: spreading out as wide as possible
a rough surface covered in bumps
items.e: Streamlined shapes reduce air and water resistance.

items.q: Why does a sheet of paper fall more slowly than the same paper screwed into a ball?
c: The flat sheet has more air resistance.
Gravity does not pull flat paper.
The ball has more air resistance.

items.q: A cyclist rides forwards. Which way does air or water resistance act on it?
c: it does not act at all
items.e: Resistance always acts against the movement.

items.q: Why is it harder to run through water than through air?

items.q: Why does a parachute slow a skydiver down?

items.e: Streamlined shapes reduce air and water resistance.

items.q: How is a fish designed or adapted to go fast?

items.e: Streamlined shapes reduce air and water resistance.

items.q: Which forces act on a falling parachute?
c: gravity pulling down and air resistance pushing up

items.q: What is air resistance?
c: a force from the air that pushes against moving objects
a force that pulls things down
